name: Financial Aid Checklist
description: A checklist for applying for financial aid and comparing award offers.

items.text: List the schools you want to receive your aid information.
Find the federal, state and school aid deadlines.
items.note: School and state deadlines are often earlier than the federal one.

items.text: Create or recover your application account and ID.
Identify whose information the forms require.
Estimate your costs and expected aid need.
Add every deadline to your calendar.
Collect identification and Social Security details.
Gather tax returns and income records.
Compile bank and investment statements.
Record any benefits or untaxed income.
Note family size and household details.
Confirm the exact document list with your aid authority.
Start the FAFSA as soon as it opens.
Enter your information accurately and completely.
Add every school that should receive your data.
Have a parent provide details and sign if required.
Review for errors before you submit.
Submit and save your confirmation.
Complete any state aid applications.
Fill out school-specific aid forms if required.
Apply for grants you may qualify for.
Search and apply for scholarships.
Look into work-study opportunities.
Keep copies of every form you submit.
Check your application status after submitting.
Respond quickly to any requests for documents.
Complete verification if your file is selected.
Correct any errors flagged on your results.
Confirm each school received your information.
Watch for and read your award notifications.
Separate grants and scholarships from loans on each offer.
Calculate the net cost after free aid at each school.
Compare total out-of-pocket cost across schools.
Understand any loan terms before accepting.
items.note: Borrow only what you need and confirm repayment terms.

items.text: Check whether aid is renewable in future years.
Accept your aid and meet any acceptance deadlines.

faq.q: When should I apply for financial aid?
faq.a: Apply as soon as the application opens for the year. Much aid is awarded on a first-come, first-served basis, and schools and states set their own earlier deadlines, so applying early protects your access to limited funds.

faq.q: What documents do I need for the FAFSA?
faq.a: You'll typically need identification, tax returns and income records, bank and investment statements, and records of any benefits. Specific requirements vary, so confirm the current list with your official aid authority.

faq.q: Do I have to accept all the aid I'm offered?
faq.a: No. You can accept grants and scholarships you qualify for and choose whether to accept work-study or loans. Borrow only what you need and understand the terms before accepting any loan.

faq.q: How do I compare financial aid award offers?
faq.a: Look at the net cost after grants and scholarships, not the sticker price. Separate free aid from loans, compare total out-of-pocket cost across schools, and factor in renewability for future years.

faq.q: Can I download this checklist as a PDF?
faq.a: Yes. Print the checklist or download the PDF and tick off each step as you apply for aid and compare offers.
